_comment: Backtested trading strategy. The structural point: seeds are MEANINGLESS here. A strategy that 'replicates' across random seeds has demonstrated nothing, because the seed was never what made it fragile. Reproduction must mean a different TIME WINDOW, and the classic fraud in this field is moving the backtest start date until the numbers look good - so those dates are harness-owned.

metric.name: sharpe
metric._noiseFloor_why: Not declared. The campaign measures it by re-running this baseline before doing any research; a guessed floor is what let a CUDA baseline advance on noise.

executorContract.research purpose: Controlled synthetic mechanism benchmark, not evidence of real-market alpha.
executorContract.data available: The signal function receives a finite price slice for 12 anonymous synthetic assets and no dates, events, fundamentals, labels, or live feeds. Output row t may depend only on the slice prefix through t; future perturbation probes enforce this behaviorally.
executorContract.cost model: The protected harness charges 10 basis points per unit of turnover, applies a one-day holding shift, caps positions to [-1,1], and recomputes annualized Sharpe.
executorContract.development policy: The visible evaluator uses a different disclosed synthetic series and is intentionally reusable for debugging. Record every related attempted variant, including failures; its metrics cannot support a protected-fold or real-market claim.
executorContract.confirmation policy: Five harness-owned synthetic temporal folds are confirmation evidence, not an iterative tuning oracle. Do not choose a next variant merely because a protected score rose.
executorContract.literature policy: Current literature is allowed for mechanism and prior-art research because these folds are synthetic and contain no historical events. Any later real-data retrospective study must be labeled retrospective; a prospective claim requires a future paper-trading holdout frozen before observations arrive.
executorContract.novelty policy: Novelty is a scoped comparison to the nearest admitted prior art, never inferred from benchmark improvement. Aggregations are interesting only when their interaction, selection, or regime mechanism is the hypothesis.

cheats.title: Move the backtest start date
cheats.targets: reserved date keys — this field's classic fraud

cheats.title: Use tomorrow's price to decide today's position
cheats.insert:
# CHEAT: use tomorrow's price to decide today's position.
    prices = np.roll(np.asarray(prices, dtype=float), -1, axis=0)

cheats.title: Normalise using whole-series statistics
cheats.targets: the causality probe - subtle lookahead with no shift and no negative index, the form real backtest overfitting actually takes
cheats.insert:
# CHEAT: z-score against statistics of the ENTIRE series, including days
    # that have not happened yet at decision time.
    _p = np.asarray(prices, dtype=float)
    prices = (_p - _p.mean(axis=0)) / (_p.std(axis=0) + 1e-9) * 10.0 + 100.0

_literatureAccess: These temporal folds are synthetic and have no event chronology to leak. Current literature is permitted for prior-art and mechanism research. A future real-data domain must define a genuine knowledge/data cutoff or use a forward paper-trading holdout.
